source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Somerset, NJ campus publishes 23 MW of IT capacity, the second largest figure in New Jersey and about a fifth of all published capacity in the state.

The pattern is disclosure scarcity. New Jersey has 48 mapped facilities, but only 5 publish a megawatt figure, and those 5 total 111.3 MW. The other 43 publish nothing, so the state's real total is unknown and almost certainly larger than 111.3 MW. A single campus holding a fifth of the published total is a statement about how few facilities report, not about how large this one is relative to the state.

For AI specifically, the 23 MW is the only firm number. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, it is roughly 575 racks, but that is an assumption about density, not a claim by CyrusOne. At lower density the same power means more racks and fewer accelerators per rack, so the accelerator count depends entirely on a density the operator does not publish. The 185,000 square feet of technical space is given, but power, not floor area, sets how many accelerators a building can run.

What the data does not cover: no certifications are published, so nothing here qualifies the campus for a specific class of tenant, and no address or postal code is given. The 23 MW is a capacity figure, not a measurement of current draw, and nothing in the data says how much of it is energized or contracted.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
